energy-ceasefire-collapse.title: Ukraine ends energy pause; Zelenskyy says 'we're done' with Trump ceasefire
energy-ceasefire-collapse.summary: President Zelenskyy told the Financial Times Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after a three-day pause requested by Washington. He said Russia struck Ukrainian energy infrastructure (Kyiv cited ~40 ballistic missiles in one assault) while Ukraine held fire. Russia said Ukraine hit a Ryazan-region refinery early Thursday. Zelenskyy also cited alleged limits on Starlink/Starshield mobility and reduced missile-warning intel; SpaceX's Musk said Starshield is US-government controlled. Trump's Sunday 'energy ceasefire' was tied to a US purchase of Russian diesel meant to ease US fuel prices before midterms.

analysis.text: Stated US goal was protecting energy infrastructure and cutting fuel prices; actual bargain mixed a diesel import deal with Moscow and pressure on Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refining. Collapse raises diesel/oil risk again and deepens Kyiv–Washington trust fracture ahead of Nov 3.

causes.why: Unilateral US energy ceasefire announcement failed when Russia kept striking Ukrainian energy and Kyiv ended its pause
US–Russia diesel deal was the political quid for pressing Kyiv to halt refinery strikes

houthis-saudi-oct15.title: Saudi coalition says cruise missile intercepted over Medina; Houthis keep targeting oil and airports
houthis-saudi-oct15.summary: On Oct 15 the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a cruise missile over the Medina region; Houthis called the claim a lie. On Oct 14 Houthis vowed more attacks on Saudi airports and oil after a strike that sources said heavily damaged Aramco's Dhahran HQ (Saudi Energy Ministry: limited fire). Riyadh King Khalid airport was hit Oct 10 (13 killed). Saudi-led strikes hit Sanaa-area fuel sites. Houthis swept to Bab el-Mandeb in September; Saudi-backed forces later pressed toward Mokha.

analysis.text: Stated Houthi motive is retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen; as Iran's proxy they open a second chokepoint (Bab el-Mandeb) while Hormuz burns, multiplying oil and Red Sea shipping risk without Tehran owning every shot.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct Houthi campaign against Saudi oil and airports
Same Iran-linked Gulf crisis: Hormuz pressure plus Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb second front

kabila-frn-succeeds-afc.title: Kabila's FRN dissolves AFC/M23 umbrella, claims Doha peace commitments
kabila-frn-succeeds-afc.summary: In a Goma statement dated Oct 14, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) led by ex-president Joseph Kabila said it had dissolved the Congo River Alliance (AFC) and assumed AFC's rights and Doha-process obligations. FRN was launched Oct 12 with M23 figures (incl. Sultani Makenga) as deputies. UN envoy Huang Xia told the Security Council a 'window of opportunity' remains via US- and Qatar-led tracks; illicit mineral trade still funds armed groups. M23 still holds Rubaya (~15% of world coltan).

analysis.text: Stated aim is national refoundation and honoring Doha; actual move consolidates Kabila's open leadership of the Rwanda-accused M23 mineral machine while keeping a diplomatic off-ramp. US–DRC minerals pact and AI/electronics demand make Rubaya leverage real.

causes.why: FRN is the formal successor structure to the Oct 12 Kabila–M23 coalition announcement

gfs-pride-sunk.title: Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sinks in Hormuz after projectile strike
gfs-pride-sunk.summary: The Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by an unidentified projectile; all 21 crew were evacuated uninjured (Singapore MPA). UKMTO had reported the attack Tuesday; sister ship GFS Giselle was damaged. IRGC claimed a naval mine on an 'unauthorised' route; maritime firm Marisks said there is no independent evidence of mining. Reuters quoted Iranian officials saying Tehran is changing shipping tactics to keep oil prices high ahead of the Nov 3 US midterms. More than 20 vessels have been attacked this month in Hormuz, the Gulf and Gulf of Oman (UKMTO).

analysis.text: Stated motive is enforcing Iran's transit rules after the US blockade; real leverage is midterm oil-price pressure and forcing Washington to trade sanctions/blockade relief for shipping safety. Expanding beyond tankers to containers raises insurance and rerouting costs globally.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct surge in Iranian strikes on commercial shipping

pla-patrol-oct14-15.title: Taiwan tracks 15 PLA aircraft and 10 PLAN ships; median-line crossings continue
pla-patrol-oct14-15.summary: Taiwan's MND reported that from 06:00 Oct 14 to 06:00 Oct 15 it tracked 15 PLA aircraft, 10 PLAN ships and seven official ships; 13 aircraft crossed the median line into northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ sectors. On Oct 14 alone it had reported 13 sorties with 11 median-line crossings during a 'joint combat readiness patrol.' China's announced live-fire window runs Oct 12–17.

analysis.text: Stated PLA framing is routine combat readiness; pressure after Lai's speech keeps Taiwan and US allies reacting while China retains rare-earth and chip-supply leverage into the Nov 10 control-suspension date.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct 12–17 live-fire / readiness patrol cycle after Lai's speech

energy-ceasefire.title: Russia spares Ukrainian energy for first time since Trump's 'energy ceasefire', pounds cities
energy-ceasefire.summary: Overnight into Oct 13, Russia struck cities and transport, killing at least four in Kharkiv, but hit no energy targets. On Oct 12 it had struck six energy sites. Neither side has confirmed the ceasefire, and the Kremlin rejected a 60-day truce.

analysis.text: The pause is fragile and unverifiable heading into winter.

diesel-deal.title: US hopes Russian diesel deal can 'soften' Moscow on peace talks
diesel-deal.summary: Witkoff and Kushner told Ukrainian officials that a deal for Russia to supply more than 2.25M barrels of diesel could revive talks, and urged Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries. Zelensky called it a 'gift to Putin.'

analysis.text: High oil prices from the Gulf war give Russia energy leverage over US policy.

causes.why: Embargo rerouted Russian products and created today's leverage
Price-cap regime shapes Russian product sales

houthis-hit-aramco.title: Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports and oil after hitting Aramco HQ
houthis-hit-aramco.summary: On Oct 14 the Houthis vowed to keep striking Saudi airports and oil facilities, a day after a strike sources say badly damaged Aramco headquarters in Dhahran. An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed 13. The Houthis call this retaliation for Saudi backing of Yemeni government forces.

analysis.text: Iran gets a deniable second front against Gulf energy, while the Houthis pursue their own goal of holding the Red Sea coast and its revenue.

causes.why: Same Houthi playbook of striking Aramco to coerce Riyadh
De-escalation of 2022 never became a settlement

kabila-m23.title: Ex-DRC president Kabila launches coalition replacing M23-AFC
kabila-m23.summary: On Oct 13 Joseph Kabila launched a new political-military coalition to replace M23-AFC, which holds large areas of eastern DRC, including Goma.

analysis.text: Defections from the Congolese army and a collapse of the US/Qatar peace tracks are the main risks.

hormuz-attacks-surge.title: Iran steps up Hormuz surveillance as tanker attacks soar and oil flows crash
hormuz-attacks-surge.summary: Iran deployed new units to watch the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler counted 10 tankers struck Sep 28–Oct 4; UKMTO counted 15 attacks Oct 6–14 (11 in the last four days). Flows fell from ~20.8M bbl on Oct 8 to 2.9M on Oct 11 (pre-war average 17.1M/day). The US keeps up its blockade of Iranian ports.

analysis.text: Iran is using control of the strait as bargaining leverage for sanctions relief, its frozen assets and an end to the blockade.

causes.why: OPEC+/Saudi oil leverage and US–Gulf friction persisted into the 2026 Gulf crisis

pla-drills.title: PLA live-fire drills in five sea areas after Lai speech; 11 aircraft cross median line
pla-drills.summary: China set drills Oct 12–17 in five sea areas while attacking President Lai's speech. Taiwan's MND reported 13 aircraft on Oct 14, 11 of which crossed the median line. China is also reportedly slowing germanium and quartz exports to Taiwan.

analysis.text: This is calibrated coercion rather than a sign of imminent action.

causes.why: 2022 drills set the template for encirclement exercises

pla-drills.unplaced: The drills were five sea areas, not one point.

kirovohrad-drone-barrage.summary: Kirovohrad region suffered its largest Russian attack of the war overnight: 360+ drones hit 26 locations, killing three and wounding six (Gov. Andriy Raikovych). Ukraine's air force said 580 drones were launched nationwide, 536 shot down.

analysis.text: Strikes of this scale on infrastructure are the stated reason Kyiv abandoned the energy pause; expect tit-for-tat refinery and grid strikes to resume at pace.

houthis-hit-aden-palace.title: Houthi missiles hit Aden presidential palace, killing five
houthis-hit-aden-palace.summary: Houthis fired missiles and drones at Aden's Al-Maashiq presidential palace complex, seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, killing five and wounding 16 (Yemeni health minister). The PM and cabinet were safe. It is the first strike on the palace in the current Houthi-Saudi conflict. The coalition said Houthis made 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid airport this month (17 killed, 333 wounded); ICAO's council condemned attacks on Saudi civil aviation.

causes.why: Escalation of the Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies

analysis.text: Hitting the government seat signals the Houthis will widen the war beyond Saudi territory to the Yemeni government itself, raising pressure on the Mokha/Bab el-Mandeb front and on Riyadh to escalate or negotiate.

trump-disgrace-eu-summit.title: Trump calls Kyiv's refinery strikes a 'disgrace' as EU summit rallies around Zelenskiy
trump-disgrace-eu-summit.summary: Trump told Newsmax that Ukraine's resumed strikes on Russian refineries are 'a disgrace' that push world oil prices higher. EU leaders hosted Zelenskiy at their Brussels summit on Oct 16, where he sought a 'winter package' of energy, air defence and funding. Ukraine's finance minister puts the unfunded 2027 budget gap at $32.6 billion, excluding about $40 billion in direct military supplies. Putin said the refinery strikes caused 'nothing particularly significant'. A Putin decree dated Oct 15 (No. 738) placed Russian units of Tarkett, Menshen, Ontex, Kappa Rus (Swedish-owned) and a Sonoco-linked packaging firm under temporary state-appointed management.

causes.why: Kyiv's exit from the energy pause and new refinery strikes drew Trump's rebuke
EU leaders object to the US-Russia diesel deal that underpins Washington's pressure on Kyiv

analysis.text: Washington's operative goal is lower pump prices before the Nov 3 midterms; Europe's is keeping Ukraine solvent and lit through winter without dependable US cover. The asset seizures signal that any EU move on frozen Russian state assets will be answered in kind against European companies still inside Russia.

lutsk-blackout-volyn.title: Russian drones black out Lutsk and Volyn; three killed in Kharkiv
lutsk-blackout-volyn.summary: Russian drone strikes on Volyn region, which borders Poland, left 370,000 people without power on Oct 16 (Reuters, citing local authorities); Lutsk lost electricity and city services ran on backup power. Russian drone strikes on Kharkiv killed three people, and DTEK reported emergency power cuts in Kyiv.

causes.why: Same Russian campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure, now reaching the west

analysis.text: Hitting the far west signals that no part of Ukraine's grid is out of reach heading into winter, which strengthens Kyiv's ask in Brussels for air defence alongside money.

gulf-of-oman-tanker-fires.title: Second tanker in a day burns in Iran's declared 'prohibited zone'; Cape Dao sinks
gulf-of-oman-tanker-fires.summary: Iran's navy said an unnamed oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems caught fire in the Gulf of Oman while crossing the zone the IRGC declared prohibited in September; it gave no cause, flag or crew status, and CENTCOM did not immediately comment. Euronews called it the second such incident in 24 hours. The bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck by a projectile on Sept 23, sank on Oct 14. Kpler said intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower.

causes.why: Continuation of the October campaign against shipping on the Hormuz approaches

analysis.text: Tehran is running a permission regime on the approaches rather than a full closure: transit on Iran's terms is the leverage it is trading against the US blockade of its ports.

gulf-of-oman-tanker-fires.unplaced: Iran said only that the tanker was east of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf of Oman; no position given.

saudi-blames-iran-eu-gcc-postponed.title: Saudi Arabia blames Iran for Houthi escalation; EU-GCC summit in Riyadh postponed
saudi-blames-iran-eu-gcc-postponed.summary: The GCC and the EU postponed indefinitely the second EU-GCC summit set for Oct 24 in Riyadh, citing Houthi attacks and the closure of King Khalid International Airport. Saudi deputy minister Rayed Krimly told reporters Iran is encouraging the Houthi escalation, that the Houthis refused a July meeting in Oman, that Riyadh has not asked for Iranian mediation, and that some Iranian and Houthi capabilities or intelligence come from 'elements in Russia or China'. AP reported at least 19 killed; the coalition said the Riyadh airport was targeted 20 times this month.

causes.why: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and oil sites made the summit unsafe to host
The widening Houthi campaign sharpened Riyadh's public case against Tehran

analysis.text: Riyadh is building the case for more US military help and for keeping Iran's Yemen card inside any US-Iran deal, while keeping its own line to Tehran open. Losing the summit dents the kingdom's safe-hub pitch to investors.

coreweave-ai-credit-shock.title: CoreWeave debt scare jolts AI trade; Treasuries rally despite hot inflation
coreweave-ai-credit-shock.summary: Yields on CoreWeave's junk-rated 2031 bonds rose to about 16% and its default-insurance cost to roughly 1,000 basis points (Reuters); the company has about $50 billion of debt (LSEG). Nvidia's Jensen Huang said CoreWeave's finances are improving and no backstop is needed; Nvidia has agreed to buy its unsold capacity through April 2032. South Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 8% and the Nikkei about 5% on Oct 15 before rebounding about 3% and 1.5% on Oct 16. The US 10-year yield fell 10.2bp to 5.086%, its biggest one-day drop in over a year, even as September PPI rose 6.3% year on year against a 5.3% consensus.

causes.why: Energy-driven inflation keeps long yields high, raising financing costs for leveraged AI builders

analysis.text: The AI build-out runs on credit. With 10-year yields above 5%, held up partly by war-driven energy inflation, the most leveraged borrowers crack first. This is where the Hormuz shock meets the AI-compute storyline.

coreweave-ai-credit-shock.unplaced: Market-wide credit move; no event site.

pla-patrol-oct15-16.title: Taiwan tracks 8 PLA sorties, all across the median line, plus 9 navy and 7 official ships
pla-patrol-oct15-16.summary: Taiwan's defence ministry detected 8 PLA aircraft sorties, 9 PLAN ships and 7 official ships around Taiwan from 6 a.m. Oct 15 to 6 a.m. Oct 16 (UTC+8). All 8 sorties crossed the median line into the northern and southwestern ADIZ.

causes.why: Continued pressure after the post-Lai-speech drills

analysis.text: Fewer aircraft but every sortie across the median line, with coast-guard-type 'official ships' present, fits Beijing's normalisation of pressure rather than a surge.

pla-patrol-oct15-16.unplaced: Activity spread across Taiwan's northern and southwestern ADIZ; no single point.

rare-earth-nov10.title: China's rare-earth leverage: Nov 10 suspension deadline, US refiners blacklisted
rare-earth-nov10.summary: China's April 2025 controls on 7 rare earths remain in force; the Oct 2025 expansion is suspended until Nov 10, 2026. On Oct 3, MP Materials and USA Rare Earth were barred from dual-use inputs. Per CFR, supplies to Japan were cut to near zero in 2026. The Oct 9 EU–China outcome promises fast-track licences without volumes or dates.

analysis.text: China treats mineral licensing as a strategic deterrent, including on Taiwan.

causes.why: Chinese mineral controls answer US chip controls

rare-earth-nov10.unplaced: The measures span China, the United States, and Japan. No single place is named.

2022-06-13-bunagana.summary: M23 rebels, whose 2022 resurgence Kinshasa blames on Rwanda, captured the border town of Bunagana.

2022-03-31-spr-release.summary: The White House announced a release of about 1 million barrels a day for six months from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

2022-10-07-bis-controls.summary: The Commerce Department restricted exports of advanced AI chips, chipmaking tools and US-person support to Chinese fabs.

2026-03-13-kharg-strike.title: US bombs military sites on Kharg Island, Iran's oil export hub
2026-03-13-kharg-strike.summary: US aircraft struck missile and mine storage sites on Kharg Island, which handles about 90% of Iran's crude exports. Officials said oil infrastructure was left intact on purpose, and Trump warned it could be hit if Iran kept interfering with Hormuz shipping.

causes.why: Escalation to pressure Iran over Hormuz

analysis.text: Washington held Iran's oil lifeline hostage instead of destroying it, a bargaining chip for reopening Hormuz.

2026-02-28-iran-war-begins.title: US and Israel strike Iran and kill Khamenei; Iran hits back and bars Hormuz
2026-02-28-iran-war-begins.summary: The US and Israel launched strikes on Iranian military and leadership targets (the US called it Operation Epic Fury), and Iranian state media confirmed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed. Iran fired missiles and drones at Israel and US bases in the Gulf, and ships were told by VHF that Hormuz transit was 'banned'.

causes.why: The crackdown framed the regime as brittle and gave Washington a political case
With no nuclear deal since 2022, force became the default tool

analysis.text: The aim looks like regime decapitation more than counter-proliferation. Iran's answer, closing Hormuz, turned a regional war into a global energy shock.

2026-03-02-hezbollah-joins-war.title: Hezbollah joins the war; Israel invades southern Lebanon
2026-03-02-hezbollah-joins-war.summary: Hezbollah fired rockets and drones at Israel on Mar 2 in retaliation for Khamenei's killing. Israel resumed heavy strikes and sent ground troops into southern Lebanon. By Mar 24 its defence minister said the army would occupy a swathe of the south.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Timeline of the Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2 March 2026 – present)

2022-02-26-swift-cbr.summary: The US, EU, UK and Canada moved to remove selected Russian banks from SWIFT and to block the Russian central bank from using its foreign reserves.

sources.name: Wikipedia: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War

effects.why: Rouble payment demand answered the reserve freeze

2022-02-17-france-leaves-mali.title: France and allies announce military withdrawal from Mali
2022-02-17-france-leaves-mali.summary: France and European partners announced the withdrawal of Operation Barkhane and Task Force Takuba from Mali, citing obstruction by the junta.

causes.why: Junta's turn to Wagner made the French presence untenable

yanbu-missile-intercepted.title: Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's Hormuz bypass, is intercepted
yanbu-missile-intercepted.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile over Yanbu, the Red Sea terminus of a major oil pipeline, plus two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones over southern Saudi Arabia and Riyadh; initial reports indicated no damage. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei rejected any role and offered to mediate. The UN Security Council condemned the Houthi attacks on Oct 15. analysis.text: Part of the swing to the right that carried into Colombia and Brazil in 2026.

2022-04-shanghai-lockdown.title: Shanghai's two-month COVID lockdown snarls supply chains
2022-04-shanghai-lockdown.summary: Shanghai locked down from late March to June 2022 under zero-COVID, disrupting ports and factories.

revisions.why: 2020 backfill: link to earlier causes

2023-01-08-china-reopens.title: China reopens its borders, ending zero-COVID after an explosive outbreak
2023-01-08-china-reopens.summary: Beijing scrapped quarantine for arrivals after abruptly abandoning zero-COVID in December. The reopening rebound faded within months amid the property slump.

causes.why: End of the zero-COVID regime begun in 2020

revisions.why: 2020 backfill: link to earlier causes

2024-07-28-venezuela-stolen-election.title: Maduro claims victory in Venezuela's election; the opposition's tallies show González won
2024-07-28-venezuela-stolen-election.summary: The electoral council declared Maduro the winner without detailed results. The opposition led by María Corina Machado published precinct tallies showing a large win for Edmundo González, who later fled into exile, while a crackdown followed.

causes.why: US engagement with Maduro since 2022 failed to produce a fair vote

2024-01-28-tower-22.title: Drone attack on Tower 22 in Jordan kills three US soldiers
2024-01-28-tower-22.summary: An Iran-backed Iraqi militia coalition, the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, struck the US outpost, killing three soldiers and wounding dozens, the first US deaths from enemy fire in the region since the Gaza war began. The US retaliated in Iraq and Syria in February.
2024-01-28-tower-22.unplaced: Tower 22 is a remote outpost; no place entity.

2024-03-22-crocus-attack.title: Islamic State gunmen kill more than 140 at Moscow's Crocus City Hall
2024-03-22-crocus-attack.summary: Four gunmen linked to ISIS-K attacked a sold-out concert and set the hall on fire. It was the deadliest attack in Russia in two decades. The Kremlin tried to link Ukraine despite IS's claim.

2024-06-19-putin-kim-treaty.title: Putin and Kim sign a mutual-defence pact in Pyongyang
2024-06-19-putin-kim-treaty.summary: The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership treaty commits each side to give military aid if the other is attacked. It was the strongest Moscow–Pyongyang tie since the Cold War.

2024-10-18-dprk-troops-to-russia.title: South Korea says North Korea is sending troops to fight for Russia
2024-10-18-dprk-troops-to-russia.summary: Seoul's intelligence service said thousands of North Korean special forces had been shipped to Russia. More than 11,000 were eventually sent, and they fought in Kursk from December.

causes.why: Russia needed troops to retake Kursk

2024-11-05-trump-elected.title: Donald Trump wins the US presidency again
2024-11-05-trump-elected.summary: Trump beat Kamala Harris and won the popular vote, while Republicans took both houses of Congress. He promised sweeping tariffs and an end to the Ukraine war.

2024-11-06-german-coalition-collapses.title: Germany's coalition collapses as Scholz fires Lindner over the debt brake
2024-11-06-german-coalition-collapses.summary: Scholz sacked FDP Finance Minister Christian Lindner after a clash over borrowing, ending the three-party coalition and leading to a February 2025 election.

2025-03-18-germany-debt-brake.title: Bundestag loosens Germany's debt brake for defence and a €500bn infrastructure fund
2025-03-18-germany-debt-brake.summary: The Bundestag voted 512–206 to change the constitution, exempting defence spending above 1% of GDP from borrowing limits and creating a €500bn infrastructure fund, as Friedrich Merz prepared to take office.

causes.why: Doubts over the US commitment pushed Berlin to spend
Coalition broke over the debt brake

analysis.text: This was Europe's largest fiscal pivot toward rearmament since the Cold War, and it made the later 5% NATO pledge credible for Germany.

2025-03-18-germany-debt-brake.unplaced: A Bundestag vote; Berlin has no place entity yet.

revisions.why: 2024 backfill: link to 2024 causes

2025-09-10-scarborough-nature-reserve.title: China declares a 'nature reserve' at Scarborough Shoal; Manila protests
2025-09-10-scarborough-nature-reserve.summary: China's State Council approved a Huangyan Island national nature reserve covering about 3,524 hectares of the shoal. The Philippines filed a diplomatic protest on Sep 12, calling it a pretext for occupation.

2024-06-04-modi-loses-majority.title: Modi wins a third term but the BJP loses its majority
2024-06-04-modi-loses-majority.summary: In results declared on Jun 4, the BJP fell to 240 of 543 seats and needed allies such as the TDP and JD(U) to form a government, a setback after a decade of single-party rule.

2025-10-14-madagascar-coup.title: Madagascar's military seizes power after Gen Z protests; president impeached
2025-10-14-madagascar-coup.summary: After youth protests over water and power cuts, Col. Michael Randrianirina's CAPSAT unit sided with the protesters. President Rajoelina fled and was impeached, and Randrianirina declared a takeover and was sworn in on Oct 17, promising elections within two years.

2025-08-29-indonesia-protests.title: Deadly riots shake Indonesia after a police vehicle kills a delivery driver; Sri Mulyani is ousted
2025-08-29-indonesia-protests.summary: Protests over lawmakers' housing allowances turned into nationwide riots after a police armoured vehicle ran over delivery driver Affan Kurniawan in Jakarta. Looters hit homes including Finance Minister Sri Mulyani's. On Sep 8 Prabowo replaced her with Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa, who promised faster growth.

analysis.text: Losing a trusted finance minister and turning to growth-first policy fed the investor doubts behind MSCI's 2026 actions.

2025-02-18-riyadh-us-russia-talks.title: US and Russia hold first high-level talks since the invasion in Riyadh; Istanbul follows
2025-02-18-riyadh-us-russia-talks.summary: Rubio, Waltz and Witkoff met Lavrov and Ushakov without Ukraine. They agreed to restore embassy operations and appoint teams on ending the war. A Feb 27 Istanbul round dealt with embassy staffing and banking.

2025-02-28-oval-office-clash.title: Trump and Vance berate Zelenskyy in the Oval Office; minerals deal unsigned
2025-02-28-oval-office-clash.summary: An Oval Office meeting broke down as Trump and Vice President Vance clashed with Zelenskyy over diplomacy with Russia. Zelenskyy left early, and the planned signing of a minerals agreement was cancelled.

2025-01-07-trump-greenland-panama.title: Trump won't rule out force to take Greenland and the Panama Canal
2025-01-07-trump-greenland-panama.summary: At a Mar-a-Lago news conference, President-elect Trump refused to rule out military or economic coercion to gain control of Greenland and the Panama Canal, calling both vital to US security, and threatened Denmark with tariffs. Denmark and Panama rejected any transfer of control.

analysis.text: This opened a year-long US campaign of territorial pressure on an ally that ended in the 2026 Greenland treaty.

2025-02-20-cartels-fto.title: US designates eight cartels and gangs as terrorist organisations
2025-02-20-cartels-fto.summary: The State Department designated Tren de Aragua, MS-13, the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG and four other groups as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists.

analysis.text: Treating cartels as terrorists gave the legal and political frame for the 2025 boat strikes, the Maduro operation and the El Mencho raid.

2025-09-09-israel-strikes-doha.title: Israel strikes Hamas leaders in Doha
2025-09-09-israel-strikes-doha.summary: Israel bombed a Doha compound where Hamas officials were discussing a US ceasefire proposal. Hamas said its top leaders survived but five members were killed, and Qatar said a security officer died. Qatar called it a violation of international law.

analysis.text: An Israeli strike in a US-allied Gulf capital weakened Gulf confidence in Washington's protection. Within eight days Saudi Arabia signed a defence pact with Pakistan.

2024-01-09-ecuador-internal-conflict.title: Ecuador declares an 'internal armed conflict' against gangs after a TV studio is stormed
2024-01-09-ecuador-internal-conflict.summary: After Los Choneros boss Fito escaped and gunmen took over a live TV broadcast in Guayaquil, President Noboa designated 22 gangs as terrorists and deployed the army.

2024-02-08-pakistan-election.title: Pakistan election: Khan-backed independents win the most seats but Sharif forms the government
2024-02-08-pakistan-election.summary: With Khan jailed and his PTI stripped of its symbol, independents backed by the PTI won 93 seats, more than PML-N's 75 and PPP's 54. Amid rigging allegations, PML-N and PPP formed a coalition and Shehbaz Sharif returned as PM in March.

2025-01-17-khan-al-qadir-conviction.title: Imran Khan gets 14 years in the Al-Qadir Trust case
2025-01-17-khan-al-qadir-conviction.summary: The court convicted Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi (seven years) over land allegedly received from a property tycoon. It added to his existing sentences and kept him in prison.
2025-01-17-khan-al-qadir-conviction.unplaced: Verdict delivered at Adiala jail, Rawalpindi.

2023-05-20-bakhmut-falls.title: Wagner claims Bakhmut after the war's longest battle
2023-05-20-bakhmut-falls.summary: Prigozhin declared full control of the ruined city after about ten months of fighting that cost both sides heavily, while feuding publicly with Russia's defence ministry.

2022-09-30-burkina-coup2.title: Second Burkina coup: Capt. Ibrahim Traoré ousts Damiba
2022-09-30-burkina-coup2.summary: Junior officers led by Ibrahim Traoré overthrew Damiba; some supporters waved Russian flags.

sources.name: Wikipedia: September 2022 Burkina Faso coup d'état

causes.why: Anti-French and pro-Russian current across the Sahel

2024-05-25-burkina-extends-transition.title: Burkina Faso's junta extends its rule by five years and makes Traoré eligible to run
2024-05-25-burkina-extends-transition.summary: A revised transition charter signed by Traoré set 60 more months from Jul 2 2024, renamed him 'President of Faso' and allowed him to stand in the elections that end the transition. Elections could come earlier 'if security permits'.

2024-01-25-africa-corps-burkina.title: Russia's new Africa Corps deploys to Burkina Faso as Wagner is folded into the state
2024-01-25-africa-corps-burkina.summary: The first Africa Corps contingent arrived in Ouagadougou. Run by Russia's defence ministry, it took over Wagner's Sahel role after Prigozhin's death.

causes.why: State takeover of Wagner's Africa business

2024-12-08-assad-falls.title: Assad's regime collapses as HTS-led rebels take Damascus
2024-12-08-assad-falls.summary: An 11-day offensive from Idlib took Aleppo, Hama and Homs before rebels entered Damascus. Assad fled to Moscow, ending more than five decades of family rule. HTS leader Ahmed al-Sharaa took charge.

causes.why: Hezbollah too weakened to rescue Assad

analysis.text: Iran lost its land bridge to Hezbollah, opening the way for the 2025 US embrace of al-Sharaa.

revisions.why: Phase E gap backfill: link to earlier causes

2025-03-13-kursk-exit.title: Russia retakes Sudzha as Ukraine's Kursk foothold collapses
2025-03-13-kursk-exit.summary: With North Korean troops in support and US intelligence sharing briefly paused, Russian forces pushed Ukraine out of most of the Kursk salient by mid-March and entered Sudzha. Kyiv lost its bargaining chip for talks.

causes.why: North Korean troops joined the counteroffensive

2025-04-02-liberation-day.title: 'Liberation Day': Trump invokes IEEPA for a 10% global tariff and higher 'reciprocal' rates
2025-04-02-liberation-day.summary: Executive Order 14257 declared trade deficits a national emergency under IEEPA. It imposed a 10% tariff on all countries from Apr 5 and higher country-specific rates from Apr 9, adding to the earlier IEEPA 'fentanyl' tariffs on Canada, Mexico and China.

analysis.text: Basing the tariffs on emergency powers rather than trade statutes made them fast to impose but exposed them in court. That is the weakness the Supreme Court ruled on in Feb 2026.

revisions.why: 2024 backfill: link to 2024 causes

2023-10-15-poland-tusk.title: Poland's opposition wins; Tusk returns as prime minister
2023-10-15-poland-tusk.summary: PiS came first but lost its majority, and Donald Tusk's Civic Coalition formed a government with two allies, promising to restore the rule of law and unlock EU funds.

2023-09-30-fico-wins.title: Robert Fico's Smer wins Slovakia's election on a pledge to stop arming Ukraine
2023-09-30-fico-wins.summary: Smer took 42 seats and Fico formed a government, joining Orbán as a skeptic of aid to Kyiv inside the EU.

2020-10-18-bolivia-arce.title: Morales's MAS returns to power as Luis Arce wins Bolivia's election
2020-10-18-bolivia-arce.summary: A year after the disputed 2019 vote and Evo Morales's exit, Arce won outright in the first round and the interim government's candidates conceded.

2023-11-19-milei-elected.title: Libertarian Javier Milei wins Argentina's presidency
2023-11-19-milei-elected.summary: The 'chainsaw' outsider beat Economy Minister Sergio Massa in the runoff, promising shock austerity to end triple-digit inflation. He became a leading Trump ally.

analysis.text: Opened the right-wing wave that ran through Chile, Colombia and Brazil into 2025–26.

2024-01-30-khan-convictions.title: Imran Khan gets 10- and 14-year sentences days before Pakistan's election
2024-01-30-khan-convictions.summary: Khan was sentenced to 10 years in the cypher case and 14 years in the Toshakhana case at the end of January. The cypher verdict was overturned in June 2024 and the Toshakhana term suspended in April.

2020-08-18-mali-coup.title: Mutinous soldiers oust Mali's President Keïta
2020-08-18-mali-coup.summary: After months of protests over insecurity and a disputed election, troops seized Kati base and arrested Keïta, who resigned. A junta led by Col. Assimi Goïta took power.

analysis.text: The first of the Sahel coups that ended France's mission and brought in Russia.

2021-09-05-guinea-coup.title: Special forces seize Guinea's President Alpha Condé
2021-09-05-guinea-coup.summary: Col. Mamady Doumbouya dissolved the constitution after Condé had changed it to win a third term in 2020.

2021-05-24-mali-second-coup.title: Mali's junta stages a second coup
2021-05-24-mali-second-coup.summary: Colonel Assimi Goïta's soldiers arrested the transitional president and prime minister after a reshuffle and stripped them of power, nine months after the 2020 coup.

2021-08-15-fall-of-kabul.title: Kabul falls to the Taliban as Ghani flees
2021-08-15-fall-of-kabul.summary: After taking most provincial capitals in a week, the Taliban entered Kabul and restored the Islamic Emirate. The US and allies airlifted more than 120,000 people by Aug 30.

causes.why: Doha deal weakened the Afghan forces

analysis.text: Pakistan welcomed the Taliban's return but soon faced a resurgent TTP sheltering in Afghanistan, the root of the 2025–26 war.

2021-02-01-myanmar-coup.title: Myanmar's military seizes power and detains Aung San Suu Kyi
2021-02-01-myanmar-coup.summary: On the day before the new parliament was to sit, the army declared the 2020 election invalid, proclaimed a state of emergency and handed power to Min Aung Hlaing. Armed resistance by the People's Defence Force followed the crackdown on protests.

analysis.text: The coup started the civil war that later produced Operation 1027 and the junta's 2025–26 election.

2021-05-10-gaza-war.title: Eleven-day Gaza war after clashes in Jerusalem
2021-05-10-gaza-war.summary: Protests over planned evictions in Sheikh Jarrah and police raids on Al-Aqsa led Hamas and Islamic Jihad to fire rockets on May 10. Israel bombed Gaza until a ceasefire on May 21.

analysis.text: Hamas drew the lesson that it could link Gaza to Jerusalem, a theme it later used to justify October 7.

2023-03-26-israel-judicial-protests.title: Netanyahu fires his defence minister, setting off mass protests over judicial reform
2023-03-26-israel-judicial-protests.summary: Months of protests against the coalition's plan to curb the Supreme Court peaked when Yoav Gallant was fired for urging a pause; Netanyahu then delayed the legislation.

causes.why: Netanyahu's return after the Bennett coalition fell

2020-08-13-abraham-accords.title: UAE and Israel announce normalisation; the Abraham Accords are signed with Bahrain
2020-08-13-abraham-accords.summary: Trump announced the UAE–Israel deal, in which Israel suspended annexation plans in the West Bank. Bahrain followed, and both signed at the White House on Sep 15; Sudan joined in October.

analysis.text: The accords built an Israel–Gulf security axis against Iran that survived the Gaza war.

2021-04-11-natanz-sabotage.title: Blast knocks out power at Natanz; Iran answers with 60% enrichment
2021-04-11-natanz-sabotage.summary: A remotely detonated device widely attributed to Israel destroyed the plant's power supply and damaged thousands of centrifuges as Vienna talks to revive the JCPOA began. Iran restricted IAEA access and raised enrichment.

2021-06-18-raisi-elected.title: Hardliner Ebrahim Raisi wins Iran's presidency on record-low turnout
2021-06-18-raisi-elected.summary: After the Guardian Council disqualified leading rivals, Raisi won with turnout around 49%, the lowest in the Islamic Republic's history.

2021-07-07-moise-assassinated.title: Haiti's President Jovenel Moïse is assassinated
2021-07-07-moise-assassinated.summary: Mercenaries, mostly Colombian, killed Moïse at his home in Port-au-Prince. The killing deepened a power vacuum that gangs filled.

analysis.text: The vacuum led to gang rule, the 2022 call for foreign troops and Henry's 2024 resignation.

2021-10-04-kishida-pm.title: Fumio Kishida becomes Japan's prime minister
2021-10-04-kishida-pm.summary: The former foreign minister won the LDP leadership after Suga stood down and led the party to a majority in the October election.

2021-09-20-evergrande-crisis.title: Evergrande's collapse sets off China's property crisis
2021-09-20-evergrande-crisis.summary: Shares of the world's most indebted developer plunged amid fears of contagion; it missed payments through the autumn and S&P declared it in default on Dec 17.

analysis.text: The property bust pushed China to lean on exports, feeding the trade surpluses of 2025.

2021-07-21-nord-stream-2-deal.title: US and Germany settle their dispute over Nord Stream 2
2021-07-21-nord-stream-2-deal.summary: Washington dropped efforts to block the Gazprom pipeline in exchange for German pledges to act if Russia used energy as a weapon. The line was completed in September but never entered service.

2021-03-11-american-rescue-plan.title: Biden signs the $1.9tn American Rescue Plan
2021-03-11-american-rescue-plan.summary: The COVID relief package passed without Republican votes and built on the 2020 CARES Act and December relief bill.

analysis.text: Economists later debated how much this stimulus added to the 2021–22 inflation surge.

2021-12-19-boric-elected.title: Leftist Gabriel Boric beats Kast to become Chile's youngest president
2021-12-19-boric-elected.summary: Boric, 35, won the runoff with 56%, after the 2019 protests and the 2020 vote for a new constitution.

2021-11-26-omicron.title: WHO names Omicron a variant of concern
2021-11-26-omicron.summary: Reported by South African scientists on Nov 24, the heavily mutated variant became dominant worldwide; many countries restricted travel from southern Africa.

2020-12-06-venezuela-assembly-vote.title: Maduro's allies take the National Assembly in a vote the opposition boycotted
2020-12-06-venezuela-assembly-vote.summary: The main opposition parties, including the four largest, refused to take part, citing irregularities and courts that had seized their party leaderships. The assembly was expanded to 277 seats.

2021-08-26-kabul-airport-bombing.title: ISIS-K bombing at Kabul airport kills about 170 Afghans and 13 US troops
2021-08-26-kabul-airport-bombing.summary: A suicide bomber struck crowds at the airport gates during the evacuation. A US retaliatory drone strike on Aug 29 killed ten civilians, including seven children.

2023-09-13-kim-putin-vostochny.title: Kim Jong Un meets Putin at the Vostochny Cosmodrome
2023-09-13-kim-putin-vostochny.summary: On his first trip abroad since the pandemic, Kim pledged full support for Russia's war; Western governments warned of arms deals.

analysis.text: The summit opened the arms-for-technology channel that led to North Korean troops in Kursk.

2024-07-21-biden-withdraws.title: Biden drops out of the 2024 race and endorses Kamala Harris
2024-07-21-biden-withdraws.summary: Concerns over his age grew after a poor June debate. Harris became the Democratic nominee.

2024-07-13-trump-shot.title: Trump survives an assassination attempt at a Pennsylvania rally
2024-07-13-trump-shot.summary: A 20-year-old gunman fired from a nearby rooftop, wounding Trump's ear and killing a spectator before a Secret Service sniper killed him.

2021-01-06-capitol-attack.title: Trump supporters storm the US Capitol to stop certification of Biden's win
2021-01-06-capitol-attack.summary: A mob tried to stop Congress counting the electoral votes. Five people died within 36 hours and 174 police officers were injured; Congress certified Biden's victory that night and the House impeached Trump a week later.

causes.why: Trump's false claims the election was stolen

2021-09-26-german-election.title: SPD narrowly wins Germany's post-Merkel election; Scholz forms a three-party coalition
2021-09-26-german-election.summary: The SPD took 25.7% against the CDU/CSU's record-low 24.1%. Olaf Scholz formed a coalition with the Greens and FDP and took office in December.

2023-08-05-second-thomas-shoal-water-can.title: China's coast guard water-cannons a Philippine resupply mission at Second Thomas Shoal
2023-08-05-second-thomas-shoal-water-can.summary: Chinese vessels blocked boats supplying the marines on the grounded BRP Sierra Madre, as they had in 2021, starting a run of clashes at the shoal.

2020-11-26-farmers-protest.title: Indian farmers march on Delhi against Modi's farm laws
2020-11-26-farmers-protest.summary: Unions, mainly from Punjab and Haryana, began the 'Dilli Chalo' march against three farm acts passed in September 2020 and camped on Delhi's borders for a year until the laws were repealed.

2024-02-14-prabowo-elected.title: Prabowo Subianto wins Indonesia's presidency
2024-02-14-prabowo-elected.summary: The defence minister and ex-general won with Jokowi's son Gibran as running mate and took office in October.

2023-08-09-villavicencio-killed.title: Ecuadorian presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio is assassinated
2023-08-09-villavicencio-killed.summary: The anti-corruption campaigner was shot leaving a rally in Quito eleven days before the vote, showing how far gang violence had reached into politics.

2021-06-13-bennett-government.title: Netanyahu is ousted as an eight-party coalition takes office in Israel
2021-06-13-bennett-government.summary: Naftali Bennett became prime minister in a rotation with Yair Lapid; it was the first coalition to include an Arab party. It collapsed in June 2022, paving the way for Netanyahu's return.

2021-11-02-ethiopia-emergency.title: Ethiopia declares a state of emergency as Tigrayan forces march south
2021-11-02-ethiopia-emergency.summary: With the TDF and the Oromo Liberation Army holding towns on the highway to Addis Ababa, the government gave itself sweeping powers to detain critics and conscript citizens.

2020-11-04-tigray-war.title: Abiy launches an offensive in Tigray, starting a two-year war
2020-11-04-tigray-war.summary: After accusing the TPLF of attacking a federal army base, Abiy sent troops and declared an emergency; Eritrean forces joined. Federal forces took Mekelle on Nov 28.

2022-08-04-pla-drills.title: China holds unprecedented drills encircling Taiwan
2022-08-04-pla-drills.summary: The PLA held live-fire exercises in zones around Taiwan, firing ballistic missiles over the island; Beijing also halted some US dialogues and sanctioned Pelosi.

2023-06-04-counteroffensive.summary: From early June, Western-equipped brigades attacked toward Zaporizhzhia oblast but made only small gains against deep Russian defences. By year-end the war had settled into attrition.

2023-10-07-hamas-attack.title: Hamas-led attack on southern Israel kills about 1,200 and takes 251 hostages
2023-10-07-hamas-attack.summary: Gunmen broke through the Gaza fence and attacked army posts, kibbutzim and a music festival in the deadliest day in Israel's history. Israel declared war and began bombing Gaza.

analysis.text: This was the hinge of the period: it led to the Gaza war, Hezbollah's front, the Houthi Red Sea campaign and the Iran–Israel exchanges that became the 2026 war.

2023-10-07-hamas-attack.unplaced: Communities along the Gaza border in southern Israel.

2026-02-28-iran-war-begins.title: US and Israel strike Iran and kill Khamenei; Iran hits back and bars Hormuz
2026-02-28-iran-war-begins.summary: The US and Israel launched strikes on Iranian military and leadership targets (the US called it Operation Epic Fury), and Iranian state media confirmed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed. Iran fired missiles and drones at Israel and US bases in the Gulf, and ships were told by VHF that Hormuz transit was 'banned'.

causes.why: The crackdown framed the regime as brittle and gave Washington a political case
With no nuclear deal since 2022, force became the default tool
Precedent of direct US strikes on Iran
Diplomacy closed off by the snapback

analysis.text: The aim looks like regime decapitation more than counter-proliferation. Iran's answer, closing Hormuz, turned a regional war into a global energy shock.

2023-10-10-avdiivka-offensive.title: Russia launches its offensive to take Avdiivka
2023-10-10-avdiivka-offensive.summary: The assault on one of Ukraine's most fortified towns, a gateway to Donetsk city, became one of the bloodiest battles of the war.

causes.why: Russia seized the initiative after Ukraine's failed counter-offensive

2022-11-01-netanyahu-returns.summary: The right-wing camp won a Knesset majority as the far right gained, ending the Bennett–Lapid interlude; Netanyahu formed his most right-wing government in December.

2019-02-26-balakot-strike.title: India bombs Balakot in Pakistan; Pakistan downs an Indian jet the next day
2019-02-26-balakot-strike.summary: Indian jets struck an alleged JeM camp; satellite imagery suggested little was hit. Pakistan captured pilot Abhinandan Varthaman and returned him days later.

analysis.text: Balakot set the precedent of cross-border Indian strikes that India repeated on a larger scale in Operation Sindoor in 2025.

2019-06-20-global-hawk-downed.title: Iran shoots down a US Global Hawk drone; Trump calls off retaliatory strikes
2019-06-20-global-hawk-downed.summary: Iran said the drone violated its airspace near Hormuz; the US said it was over international waters. Trump approved and then cancelled strikes on IRGC sites.
2019-06-20-global-hawk-downed.unplaced: Over the Strait of Hormuz; not pinned.

2019-05-23-modi-reelected.title: Modi's BJP wins a bigger majority in India's election
2019-05-23-modi-reelected.summary: The BJP won 303 seats with 37% of the vote, the highest share for any party since 1989, weeks after the Balakot strike.

2019-02-14-pulwama-attack.title: Suicide bombing in Pulwama kills 40 Indian paramilitary police
2019-02-14-pulwama-attack.summary: A local recruit of Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed rammed a convoy on the Jammu–Srinagar highway. India blamed Pakistan, which denied involvement.

2019-05-12-fujairah-tanker-sabotage.title: Four ships are sabotaged off Fujairah as US–Iran tensions rise
2019-05-12-fujairah-tanker-sabotage.summary: Two Saudi tankers, a Norwegian tanker and an Emirati bunkering ship were holed by explosive devices; US officials blamed Iran, which denied it. In June two more tankers were attacked in the Gulf of Oman.

2019-04-21-zelensky-elected.title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy wins Ukraine's presidency in a landslide
2019-04-21-zelensky-elected.summary: The television comedian beat incumbent Petro Poroshenko with 73% in the runoff, promising to end the Donbas war.

2020-01-03-soleimani-killed.title: US drone strike kills Iran's Qasem Soleimani at Baghdad airport
2020-01-03-soleimani-killed.summary: Trump ordered the strike that killed the Quds Force commander and Iraqi militia leader Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. Iraq's parliament voted to expel US troops, and Iran vowed revenge.

analysis.text: Removing Soleimani weakened Iran's coordination of its proxy network but hardened the US–Iran confrontation that runs to the 2026 war.

2020-01-23-wuhan-lockdown.title: China locks down Wuhan as a new coronavirus spreads
2020-01-23-wuhan-lockdown.summary: Beijing sealed off Wuhan and other Hubei cities, an unprecedented quarantine of tens of millions, as the virus was already spreading abroad.

2020-01-31-brexit.title: The UK formally leaves the European Union
2020-01-31-brexit.summary: Britain left at 23:00 GMT, entering a transition period to Dec 31 during which it stayed in the single market while negotiating a trade deal.

2020-01-15-phase-one-deal.title: US and China sign the 'Phase One' trade deal
2020-01-15-phase-one-deal.summary: Trump and Vice Premier Liu He signed a truce in which China pledged to buy at least $200bn more US goods and services over 2020–21. China later bought only about 58% of the promised extra, and most tariffs stayed.

2020-01-11-tsai-reelected.title: Tsai Ing-wen wins re-election in a landslide, rebuffing Beijing
2020-01-11-tsai-reelected.summary: Tsai and running mate Lai Ching-te won with a record vote after Hong Kong's 2019 unrest, defeating the KMT's Han Kuo-yu.

2020-02-29-doha-agreement.title: US and Taliban sign the Doha deal on a full US withdrawal from Afghanistan
2020-02-29-doha-agreement.summary: Washington agreed to withdraw all troops within 14 months; the Taliban pledged not to let al-Qaeda use Afghan soil and to open talks with Kabul, which began in Doha in September. The Afghan government was not a party.

analysis.text: The deal set the timetable for the August 2021 collapse of the Afghan republic and the Taliban's return.

2020-03-05-idlib-ceasefire.title: Turkey's Operation Spring Shield hits Assad's forces; Putin and Erdoğan agree an Idlib ceasefire
2020-03-05-idlib-ceasefire.summary: After a Feb 27 airstrike killed more than 30 Turkish soldiers, Turkey launched drone strikes on Syrian government forces and shot down Syrian jets. A Moscow-brokered ceasefire froze the last rebel enclave, dominated by HTS.

analysis.text: The frozen Idlib enclave let HTS survive and rebuild, launching the 2024 offensive that toppled Assad.

2020-03-26-maduro-indicted.title: US charges Maduro with narco-terrorism and offers $15m for his arrest
2020-03-26-maduro-indicted.summary: The Justice Department indicted Maduro and 14 officials over cocaine trafficking with FARC. In May, a botched mercenary raid ('Operation Gideon') to seize him was crushed.

2020-05-15-huawei-fdpr.title: US uses the foreign direct product rule to cut Huawei off from chipmakers
2020-05-15-huawei-fdpr.summary: Commerce required licences for chips made abroad with US tools and software for Huawei. TSMC stopped taking new Huawei orders; the rule was tightened again in August.

causes.why: Tech war continued despite the trade truce

analysis.text: The FDPR became the template for the 2022 controls on China's whole chip sector.

2020-06-15-galwan-clash.title: Galwan Valley clash kills 20 Indian soldiers in the first deadly China–India border fight in decades
2020-06-15-galwan-clash.summary: Troops fought with clubs and stones in Ladakh amid a standoff that began in May. China later acknowledged four deaths. India banned dozens of Chinese apps and tightened Chinese investment rules.

analysis.text: Galwan pushed India closer to the US-led Quad while it kept buying Russian arms and oil.

2020-06-16-liaison-office-blown-up.title: North Korea blows up the inter-Korean liaison office in Kaesong
2020-06-16-liaison-office-blown-up.summary: After weeks of anger over activists' leaflet launches, voiced by Kim Yo Jong, Pyongyang demolished the joint office opened in 2018, ending the détente of the Moon–Kim summits.

2020-06-30-hong-kong-nsl.title: Beijing imposes a national security law on Hong Kong
2020-06-30-hong-kong-nsl.summary: The NPC Standing Committee passed a law criminalising secession, subversion, terrorism and collusion with foreign forces, with sentences up to life. The US ended Hong Kong's special trade status and the UK opened a path to citizenship for BN(O) holders.

analysis.text: Hong Kong's fate hardened Taiwanese opinion against 'one country, two systems'.

2020-10-03-juba-agreement.title: Sudan's transitional government signs the Juba peace deal with rebel groups
2020-10-03-juba-agreement.summary: The agreement with the Sudan Revolutionary Front promised power-sharing and integration of fighters; two major rebel groups stayed out.

2020-10-18-bolivia-arce.title: Morales's MAS returns to power as Luis Arce wins Bolivia's election
2020-10-18-bolivia-arce.summary: A year after the disputed 2019 vote and Evo Morales's exit, Arce won outright in the first round and the interim government's candidates conceded.

2020-10-23-libya-ceasefire.title: Libya's warring sides sign a permanent ceasefire in Geneva
2020-10-23-libya-ceasefire.summary: The UN-backed 5+5 military commission agreed a nationwide ceasefire and the departure of foreign fighters within three months, after Turkey's intervention broke Haftar's siege of Tripoli. Foreign forces, including Russia's Wagner, stayed.

2020-10-25-chile-plebiscite.title: Chileans vote 78% to replace Pinochet's constitution
2020-10-25-chile-plebiscite.summary: A year after mass protests, 78.27% approved drafting a new constitution and 78.99% chose a fully elected convention.

2020-11-04-tigray-war.title: Abiy launches an offensive in Tigray, starting a two-year war
2020-11-04-tigray-war.summary: After accusing the TPLF of attacking a federal army base, Abiy sent troops and declared an emergency; Eritrean forces joined. Federal forces took Mekelle on Nov 28.

2020-11-03-us-election.title: Biden defeats Trump; Trump refuses to concede
2020-11-03-us-election.summary: Biden won 306 electoral votes amid record turnout and mail voting. Trump's fraud claims were rejected by courts and culminated in the Jan 6 2021 Capitol attack.

2020-08-04-beirut-blast.title: Ammonium nitrate explosion devastates Beirut's port
2020-08-04-beirut-blast.summary: About 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate stored for years at the port detonated, killing more than 200 and wrecking much of the city amid an economic collapse. The government resigned within a week.

2020-05-07-kadhimi-pm.title: Iraq's intelligence chief Mustafa al-Kadhimi becomes PM after months of protests
2020-05-07-kadhimi-pm.summary: After protests toppled Adel Abdul-Mahdi, parliament approved Kadhimi, who promised early elections and to rein in armed groups. Iran-aligned militias distrusted him.

2019-03-23-baghuz-caliphate-ends.title: US-backed SDF takes Baghuz, ending the Islamic State's territorial caliphate
2019-03-23-baghuz-caliphate-ends.summary: The last IS enclave on the Euphrates near the Iraqi border fell after a six-week battle; tens of thousands of fighters' relatives were moved to camps such as al-Hol.

2019-09-14-abqaiq-attack.title: Drones and missiles knock out half of Saudi oil output at Abqaiq and Khurais
2019-09-14-abqaiq-attack.summary: The Houthis claimed the attack; the US and Saudi Arabia blamed Iran, and France, Germany and the UK agreed Iran was responsible. Brent briefly jumped by the most on record.

analysis.text: The muted US response convinced Riyadh it could not rely on Washington, pushing it toward détente with Iran in 2023.

2019-05-23-modi-reelected.title: Modi's BJP wins a bigger majority in India's election
2019-05-23-modi-reelected.summary: The BJP won 303 seats with 37% of the vote, the highest share for any party since 1989, weeks after the Balakot strike.

2019-07-24-johnson-pm.title: Boris Johnson becomes UK prime minister vowing Brexit 'do or die'
2019-07-24-johnson-pm.summary: Johnson replaced Theresa May, who quit after Parliament rejected her withdrawal deal three times.

2019-06-09-hong-kong-protests.title: Hong Kong's extradition-bill protests become the largest in its history
2019-06-09-hong-kong-protests.summary: Mass marches against a bill allowing extradition to mainland China grew into a months-long movement against Beijing's tightening control.
2019-06-09-hong-kong-protests.unplaced: Hong Kong's Wikipedia coordinates are a territory centroid.

2019-08-05-article-370-revoked.title: India revokes Kashmir's special status under Article 370
2019-08-05-article-370-revoked.summary: New Delhi split the state into two union territories, cut communications for months and detained Kashmiri leaders. Pakistan downgraded ties.
2019-08-05-article-370-revoked.unplaced: Constitutional order covering the whole region.

2019-02-28-hanoi-summit.title: Trump–Kim summit in Hanoi collapses without a deal
2019-02-28-hanoi-summit.summary: The second summit was cut short over North Korea's demand for sanctions relief; Trump said Kim wanted all sanctions lifted.

2019-04-11-bashir-ousted.title: Sudan's army ousts Omar al-Bashir after months of protests
2019-04-11-bashir-ousted.summary: The military ended his three-decade rule and formed a Transitional Military Council led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan with RSF chief Hemedti as deputy.

analysis.text: The Burhan–Hemedti partnership born here broke apart in the 2023 war.

2018-04-02-abiy-pm.title: Abiy Ahmed becomes Ethiopia's prime minister after years of protest
2018-04-02-abiy-pm.summary: The 41-year-old Oromo reformer freed political prisoners, opened the economy and reached out to Eritrea.

2019-01-23-guaido-interim-president.title: Juan Guaidó declares himself Venezuela's interim president; the US recognises him
2019-01-23-guaido-interim-president.summary: The opposition-led National Assembly called Maduro a usurper after his disputed 2018 re-election. The US and dozens of countries backed Guaidó; Russia, China and Cuba backed Maduro.

analysis.text: The failure of the Guaidó strategy left Washington looking for other ways to remove Maduro, up to the 2026 raid.

2019-05-10-us-china-tariffs-escalate.title: Trump raises tariffs on $200bn of Chinese goods to 25% as talks collapse
2019-05-10-us-china-tariffs-escalate.summary: The trade war that began in January 2018 escalated after negotiations broke down; China retaliated and in August the US labelled it a currency manipulator.

2019-05-15-huawei-entity-list.title: US puts Huawei on its Entity List and declares a telecoms emergency
2019-05-15-huawei-entity-list.summary: Trump's order targeted 'foreign adversary' telecoms gear, and Commerce barred US firms from supplying Huawei without a licence.

2019-05-12-fujairah-tanker-sabotage.title: Four ships are sabotaged off Fujairah as US–Iran tensions rise
2019-05-12-fujairah-tanker-sabotage.summary: Two Saudi tankers, a Norwegian tanker and an Emirati bunkering ship were holed by explosive devices; US officials blamed Iran, which denied it. In June two more tankers were attacked in the Gulf of Oman.

2019-10-11-abiy-nobel.title: Ethiopia's Abiy Ahmed wins the Nobel Peace Prize for ending the war with Eritrea
2019-10-11-abiy-nobel.summary: The committee cited his 2018 peace with Eritrea. A year later he went to war in Tigray.

2019-10-09-operation-peace-spring.title: Turkey invades northeast Syria after Trump pulls US troops back
2019-10-09-operation-peace-spring.summary: Days after Trump ordered US forces out of the area, Turkish troops and allied Syrian militias attacked the Kurdish-led SDF. More than 300,000 people fled; the SDF invited in Assad's army and Russia brokered a buffer zone.

causes.why: End of the caliphate weakened the case for US troops

2019-01-01-bolsonaro-inaugurated.title: Jair Bolsonaro is sworn in as Brazil's president
2019-01-01-bolsonaro-inaugurated.summary: The far-right former army captain took office in Brasília, beginning a presidency that ended in his 2022 defeat by Lula and a coup plot.

2019-04-11-bashir-ousted.title: Sudan's army ousts Omar al-Bashir after months of protests
2019-04-11-bashir-ousted.summary: The military ended his three-decade rule and formed a Transitional Military Council led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan with RSF chief Hemedti as deputy.

2019-07-24-johnson-pm.title: Boris Johnson becomes UK prime minister vowing Brexit 'do or die'
2019-07-24-johnson-pm.summary: Johnson replaced Theresa May, who quit after Parliament rejected her withdrawal deal three times.

2019-03-25-golan-recognition.title: Trump recognises Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights
2019-03-25-golan-recognition.summary: The US became the first country to recognise Israel's 1981 de facto annexation of territory captured from Syria in 1967.

2019-10-23-russia-africa-summit.title: Putin hosts 43 African leaders at the first Russia–Africa summit in Sochi
2019-10-23-russia-africa-summit.summary: Putin offered aid and trade 'without political conditions', the diplomatic counterpart of Wagner's growing presence on the continent.

2019-11-11-gambia-v-myanmar.title: The Gambia takes Myanmar to the World Court for genocide against the Rohingya
2019-11-11-gambia-v-myanmar.summary: Backed by the 57-member OIC, the case followed the army's 2017 expulsion of over 700,000 Rohingya; Aung San Suu Kyi defended Myanmar at The Hague in December.
2019-11-11-gambia-v-myanmar.unplaced: Filed at the ICJ in The Hague.

2019-11-24-china-cables.title: Leaked 'China Cables' expose how Xinjiang's internment camps are run
2019-11-24-china-cables.summary: The ICIJ published internal documents including an operations manual for the camps; Beijing called them fabricated.

2020-03-05-idlib-ceasefire.title: Turkey's Operation Spring Shield hits Assad's forces; Putin and Erdoğan agree an Idlib ceasefire
2020-03-05-idlib-ceasefire.summary: After a Feb 27 airstrike killed more than 30 Turkish soldiers, Turkey launched drone strikes on Syrian government forces and shot down Syrian jets. A Moscow-brokered ceasefire froze the last rebel enclave, dominated by HTS.

causes.why: Turkey's deeper military role in northern Syria

analysis.text: The frozen Idlib enclave let HTS survive and rebuild, launching the 2024 offensive that toppled Assad.

2020-08-20-navalny-poisoned.title: Navalny is poisoned with Novichok on a flight from Tomsk
2020-08-20-navalny-poisoned.summary: His plane made an emergency landing in Omsk and he was flown to Berlin, where German labs found a Novichok nerve agent. The EU imposed sanctions; he returned to Russia and was arrested in January 2021.

2020-09-27-karabakh-war.title: Azerbaijan launches the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War, with Turkish drones
2020-09-27-karabakh-war.summary: Azerbaijan's offensive, aided by Turkish Bayraktar drones and reportedly Syrian mercenaries, retook districts held by Armenia since 1994 and captured Shusha on Nov 8.

2021-07-21-nord-stream-2-deal.title: US and Germany settle their dispute over Nord Stream 2
2021-07-21-nord-stream-2-deal.summary: Washington dropped efforts to block the Gazprom pipeline in exchange for German pledges to act if Russia used energy as a weapon. The line was completed in September but never entered service.

2022-04-10-imran-khan.title: Pakistan's PM Imran Khan ousted in no-confidence vote
2022-04-10-imran-khan.summary: Imran Khan became the first Pakistani prime minister removed by a no-confidence vote.

sources.name: Wikipedia: No-confidence motion against Imran Khan

2022-10-16-party-congress.title: CCP 20th Party Congress gives Xi a third term
2022-10-16-party-congress.summary: The congress (16–22 October) cleared the way for Xi Jinping's norm-breaking third term and a loyalist Politburo Standing Committee.

sources.name: Wikipedia: 20th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party

2022-10-22-meloni-government.title: Giorgia Meloni takes office as Italy's first woman prime minister
2022-10-22-meloni-government.summary: Her Brothers of Italy-led coalition was described as the first far-right-led government in Italy since the Second World War; it kept Rome firmly behind Ukraine.

2021-11-07-nicaragua-sham-vote.title: Ortega wins a fourth straight term after jailing his rivals
2021-11-07-nicaragua-sham-vote.summary: Police arrested seven potential opposition candidates before the vote. The EU and US rejected the result.

2021-11-29-jcpoa-vienna.title: Vienna talks to revive the Iran nuclear deal resume under Raisi
2021-11-29-jcpoa-vienna.summary: Indirect US–Iran talks to restore the 2015 JCPOA resumed in Vienna, the first round under President Ebrahim Raisi's government.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action

causes.why: Iran expanded enrichment after the killing
Biden sought a return to the deal
Talks resumed under a hardline president

2021-05-10-gaza-war.title: Eleven-day Gaza war after clashes in Jerusalem
2021-05-10-gaza-war.summary: Protests over planned evictions in Sheikh Jarrah and police raids on Al-Aqsa led Hamas and Islamic Jihad to fire rockets on May 10. Israel bombed Gaza until a ceasefire on May 21.

analysis.text: Hamas drew the lesson that it could link Gaza to Jerusalem, a theme it later used to justify October 7.

2018-04-16-zte-export-ban.title: US bars American firms from selling to ZTE
2018-04-16-zte-export-ban.summary: Commerce imposed a seven-year ban for sanctions-busting sales to Iran and North Korea, nearly killing the company; Trump lifted it in July after a settlement.

2018-06-13-hodeidah-offensive.title: Saudi- and UAE-led forces assault the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah
2018-06-13-hodeidah-offensive.summary: The coalition's biggest battle of the war targeted Yemen's main aid lifeline and raised fears of famine.

2018-05-20-maduro-reelected.title: Maduro wins a second term in a vote widely called a sham
2018-05-20-maduro-reelected.summary: Major opposition parties were barred and turnout was the lowest of Venezuela's democratic era; the US, the EU and Latin American governments refused to recognise the result.

2018-05-08-us-quits-jcpoa.title: Trump withdraws the US from the Iran nuclear deal and restores sanctions
2018-05-08-us-quits-jcpoa.summary: France, Germany and Britain said the 2015 deal remained binding; US 'maximum pressure' sanctions, including on oil, were reimposed over the following months.

analysis.text: The withdrawal began the cycle of Iranian escalation, tanker attacks and nuclear expansion that ran to the 2025–26 wars.

2018-07-30-wagner-car-journalists.title: Three Russian journalists investigating Wagner are killed in the Central African Republic
2018-07-30-wagner-car-journalists.summary: They died in an ambush three days after arriving, as Russian mercenaries began guarding President Touadéra's government.
2018-07-30-wagner-car-journalists.unplaced: Ambush site outside Bangui not precisely located.

2018-08-27-un-myanmar-genocide-call.title: UN investigators call for Myanmar's generals to be tried for genocide
2018-08-27-un-myanmar-genocide-call.summary: The fact-finding mission named commander Min Aung Hlaing over the 2017 expulsion of Rohingya; Facebook removed his account.

2018-08-13-xinjiang-un-review.title: UN panel says China may be holding a million Uyghurs in camps
2018-08-13-xinjiang-un-review.summary: At a UN anti-racism committee review, members cited credible reports of mass detention in Xinjiang; Beijing first denied the camps and later called them vocational centres.
2018-08-13-xinjiang-un-review.unplaced: UN review in Geneva about camps across Xinjiang.

2018-03-04-skripal-poisoning.title: Former spy Sergei Skripal is poisoned with Novichok in Salisbury
2018-03-04-skripal-poisoning.summary: Britain blamed Russia's GRU; the UK and its allies expelled more than 150 Russian diplomats.

2018-04-23-armenia-velvet-revolution.title: Armenia's 'Velvet Revolution' ousts Serzh Sargsyan
2018-04-23-armenia-velvet-revolution.summary: Mass protests led by Nikol Pashinyan forced Sargsyan out days after he moved from president to prime minister; Pashinyan was elected PM in May.

2018-07-11-trump-nord-stream-2.title: Trump says Germany is 'captive of Russia' over Nord Stream 2
2018-07-11-trump-nord-stream-2.summary: At the NATO summit in Brussels he attacked the Baltic gas pipeline and pressed allies to spend more on defence.
